one_liner: Young C++20 JavaScript interpreter from the Solar browser project; 1.2-2.5x Duktape on v8-v7, but slower than QuickJS everywhere.
what_it_does: An experimental from-scratch ECMAScript engine (bytecode VM, no JIT for JavaScript) built as the script engine of the Solar browser; it runs DOM-free JavaScript from a console binary or as a static library. Embedding goes through one C++ header, quanta/Embed.h (Runtime, Isolate, Realm, DefineClass, DefineMethod, DOMObject native objects with Visit()), which is a different API from Duktape's C stack API, so it is not a drop-in replacement.
how_it_is_fast: A register-based bytecode VM with hybrid switch/tail-call dispatch (since 0.9.2; the tree-walking interpreter was removed), NaN-boxed 8-byte values, shared immortal Shapes for objects, butterfly-style property storage, string slices as views and lazy function-body parsing. Memory comes from a non-moving, size-class-segregated cell heap (16 KB blocks in 1 MB chunks) with a sticky-mark-bit generational collector, a write-barrier remembered set and time-sliced majors, plus conservative stack scanning; non-GC memory goes through mimalloc and RegExp through PCRE2 with its JIT enabled. Default builds are clang -O3 -march=native with ThinLTO.
when_to_use: You are replacing Duktape in a desktop host on x86-64 Linux or Windows and want about 2.2-2.5x its v8-v7 score with modern syntax, and can accept a 5-8 MB binary.

You are building a browser-like host that needs multiple realms per isolate, WindowProxy-style exotic objects, structured clone and host-driven module loading and timers, all of which Embed.h now exposes.
Compute-style scripts close to QuickJS speed: on Ubuntu it edges QuickJS on DeltaBlue, Crypto, RayTrace and NavierStokes.
MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft) suits you better than LGPL, and you are comfortable tracking a fast-moving C++20 codebase.
when_not_to_use: When QuickJS is an option: QuickJS 2026.06.04 scored higher on every platform in the same suite (1217 vs 1068 Ubuntu, 1761 vs 1118 macOS arm64, 1067 vs 941 Windows) with a binary about one fifth the size.

Allocation-heavy or long-lived-structure workloads: Quanta scores about half of QuickJS on Splay (1655 vs 3183 on Ubuntu) and well below on EarleyBoyer, and its own docs/internals/gc.md says a splay tree's garbage gets no help from minor collections.
macOS arm64: only about 1.2x Duktape by score, losing Crypto, RegExp and Splay to Duktape, with the same 46 s wall time.

Small or constrained devices and footprint-sensitive embedding: 5.3-8 MB executables against Duktape's 330-430 KB; Linux, macOS and Windows are the only documented platforms, and there is no Intl or Temporal yet (ICU4X and Temporal are on the roadmap).

Production or untrusted code: v1.0.0 shipped on 2026-09-28, 26 stars, a single main author with AI-assisted commits, the embedding API was still gaining core features on 2026-10-04/05, and no fuzzing or security policy is documented.

integration.form: static lib (build/lib/libquanta.a via ./build.sh lib or make lib, bundling PCRE2, utf8proc and mimalloc) plus a console executable; CMake build also available
integration.dependencies: vendored submodules: PCRE2 (BSD-3-Clause with exception, JIT on), utf8proc (MIT), mimalloc (MIT); no ICU
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; clang and clang++ (CMake defaults to clang because its clang-only vectorisation flags break the C libraries under GCC; ThinLTO needs lld), CMake 3.15+ if using CMake; MSVC path in CMakeLists uses /std:c++20
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows; release binaries for linux-x64, macos-arm64 and windows-x64. Default builds use -march=native; the Linux CI build uses -march=x86-64 -msse4.2 -mavx -mavx2 -mtune=haswell and the MSVC CMake path /arch:AVX2, so the CI and MSVC binaries require AVX2 (compiler and flags of the release assets are not documented)
integration.thread_safety: One Isolate per thread, any number of Realms in it; everything allocated in an Isolate belongs to its creating thread and may not move to another; a second Isolate cannot be created while one is live on the same thread

gotchas: Benchmark asymmetry: the Duktape baseline is ahaoboy/duktape-build's -Os build of unreleased master 2.99.99 (2.7.0 on Windows), while Quanta's own builds use -O3, ThinLTO and -march=native or AVX2 flags; the release binary that was measured has no documented compiler or flags, and each engine ran the v8-v7 suite once per day on unspecified GitHub runner CPUs.

The MSVC branch of CMakeLists.txt compiles with /fp:fast, although the clang branch deliberately excludes -ffast-math because it breaks IEEE 754 behaviour that JavaScript numbers require; prefer the clang build (build.sh or build-windows.bat) on Windows.

C++ members of a native object do not keep JS cells alive; only its Visit() does, and roots are found by a conservative scan of the real stack, so ASan's use-after-return mode must stay off (the Makefile notes it caused live objects to be swept). The interpreter and runtime are compiled with -fno-stack-protector on purpose; only the lexer and parser keep -fstack-protector-strong.
Values are NaN-boxed with pointers in the low 48 bits, and the RegExp engine is PCRE2 with JIT, so JavaScript RegExp execution does need executable memory even though the VM itself has no JIT.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Quanta over Duktape, njs or LibJS when you want a modern, faster-than-Duktape C++20 engine with a browser-oriented multi-realm embedding API; QuickJS is faster and smaller in the same suite, and Ant (about 1.8-2x QuickJS in the same suite) or Escargot (Intl/Temporal, wide platform support) are better picks when speed or maturity matter.
verified_claims_summary: In ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark's daily GitHub Actions run (results dated 2026-10-05; CPU models not stated), the Quanta 1.0.0 release binary scored 1068 vs 489 for an -Os Duktape 2.99.99 on Ubuntu, 1118 vs 905 on macOS arm64 and 941 vs 371 against Duktape 2.7.0 on Windows (about 2.2x, 1.2x and 2.5x, derived from page data). QuickJS 2026.06.04 beat Quanta on every platform (1217, 1761, 1067).
status_note: Very active (dozens of commits on 2026-10-04/05, v1.0.0 tagged 2026-09-28) and copyable under MPL-2.0 with permissive bundled dependencies, but experimental: a web snippet from the Solar browser site (snippet only, page blocked) says it passes about 80% of test262, and the embedding API is still changing.
